novelty.why: Replaying human economics experiments with LLMs is an established genre; the new part is testing leniency and whistleblower institutions on agents against a human benchmark. Clear problem, sensible method, but the testbed framing is still only a promise.
novelty.one_change_to_make_it_new: Show a regime ranking that flips between humans and LLMs, explain why mechanistically (told versus paid punishment), and derive one concrete policy design implication for agent markets.

positive_control.why: Above-Nash pricing in laissez-faire shows collusion can arise, but not that the harness measures regime effects correctly; three models in a pilot gives no interval.
positive_control.fix: Add an instructed-collusion arm (told to maximise joint profit) and report scripted-player rates as a table: the harness must recover known cartel, report and price rates exactly.

contamination_test.why: Asking the model about the paper is weak; models confabulate or deny. Rescaling is the right test, but 'stays the same' without a fixed equivalence margin proves nothing.
contamination_test.fix: Pre-register an equivalence margin for the rescaled rerun, add a cloze probe of the paper's published numbers, and report both with intervals next to the main result.

scorecard_30s.why: 'x of 8' is a crisp headline, but 'reproduced' has no stated rule per row, rows mix heterogeneous measures, and rows 7 and 8 vanish if arms are cut.
scorecard_30s.fix: State one reproduction rule in the caption (same direction and gap beyond the Stockholm-Rome span), mark unrun rows 'not tested', and use only tested rows as denominator.

must_have_in_report: Table per regime: independent sessions, duopolies, periods, seeds, refusals and errors, total API calls and cost.
Commit hash and timestamp of the pre-registration, provably earlier than the first logged API call.
Rescaled-payoff rerun with its pre-registered equivalence margin and the observed difference with confidence interval.
Human versus LLM table showing Stockholm and Rome separately, with cluster bootstrap intervals for the LLM values.
Scripted-player test results proving payoffs, detection rate and report logic match the paper exactly.

cut.why_cheapest: An LLM judge classifying stated motives measures text, not behaviour; unfaithful rationales make it a weak secondary result that I would discount anyway.
cut.why_most_expensive: A 'testbed' and per-model 'cartel profile' with one model is an anecdote; several providers show whether the human-LLM gap is general or a quirk of one model.
cut.order_change: Yes: cut V3 before V4, because the testbed claim needs more than one model more than it needs a dose-response curve.

biggest_risk: Inference unit: with rematching in a pool of 20, duopolies are not independent; bootstrapping over duopolies gives overly narrow intervals and overstated human-LLM differences, costing a full Execution point.
three_questions: With rematching in a pool of 20 agents, what is your independent unit for the bootstrap, and how many independent sessions does each regime get?
Which equivalence margin on the rescaled-payoff rerun counts as 'behaviour stays the same', and was it fixed before you saw the data?
How do you separate a genuine response to the fine from mere instruction-following of its description, given that punishments are only told and never felt?
